focus: verdict per skill type plus the phased plan with order, risk and rollback
answeredQuestions: Which mechanisms make each of the five routing decisions in sk-code, sk-doc, sk-design and system-deep-loop, and where is each decision restated?
Where have restated copies of the same routing decision drifted, and which copy is authoritative?
Which checks, parsers, templates, generators, benchmarks and runtime mirrors enforce the current shape, and what would each proposed change break?
Which routing shape wins for hubs, for mode packets and for standalone skills: per-mode ROUTER.md, one hub ROUTER.md, the advisor hybrid, or JSON-only?
What readability defects exist per skill, with quoted passages?
What phased implementation plan (order, risk, rollback) delivers the winning shape?

graphEvents.label: One hub ROUTER.md plus JSON stage one is the only shape no check rejects
Five phases, hub SKILL.md last because of the re-mint

label: Verdict for hubs: one hub ROUTER.md wins; per-mode ROUTER.md is unparseable (router-replay-lib.cjs:374) and forbidden by canon (parent-skill-root-router-template.md:20), hub-level JSON-only fails RRC-001 and RRC-009 (root-router-contract.cjs:127-135) and empties the reach diagnostic stage-two input (doctor-router-reach.yaml:65), so the advisor hybrid is the only shape no check rejects.

Verdict for mode packets: no ROUTER.md per mode; the machine block may stay inline or move to an appendix in the same SKILL.md because parseRouter reads the whole text (:397) and packets are outside the compiler hash, or be deleted where the hub ROUTER.md section 3 already names the leaves, as 9 of 14 sk-doc packets already demonstrate.

Verdict for standalone skills: inline SMART ROUTING stays and JSON-only does not apply, because no standalone skill carries ROUTER.md, hub-router.json or mode-registry.json (only the seven hubs do) and package_skill.py still requires the H2 section and the three marker words (:69, :182-184).

The advisor report recommendation survives its own errors with three amendments: confirmed are one hub ROUTER.md, no per-mode ROUTER.md, JSON-only only as hybrid, leaf-manifest decides nothing, parseRouter cannot see a packet-root router; to correct are about 59 aliases (really 83), the system-deep-loop stale manifest (7 of 7 fresh), and the one-way section 2 versus section 9 drift (bidirectional); missing is sk-doc 9 router-less packets, the strongest evidence that per-mode blocks are optional.

Readability verdict: the routing share of the largest packet is the problem, not the hub prose; sk-code-review/SKILL.md (730 lines) opens SMART ROUTING at 49 and the first executable step tree at 67 with resolver pseudocode running past 392, so roughly half the file is routing apparatus before the first check, while the hub files carry the same defect in miniature (sk-doc/SKILL.md:53 a 107-word definition, system-deep-loop/SKILL.md:54-58 a build invariant inside routing).

Plan phase 0: capture a baseline of compiled-route-guard.cjs --json (7 of 7 fresh today), verify-router-sync.cjs, parent-skill-check.cjs, check-rule-copies.js and package_skill.py --strict before any edit, because without it a later no-regressions claim cannot separate an old warning from a new one; risk none, rollback not applicable.

Plan phase 1: arrest drift inside JSON and inside section 2 versus section 9 first, merging the CI vocabulary to hub-router.json code-ci-aliases and making ROUTER.md section 2 and section 9 agree both ways; risk low, guarded by 3d-alias and 5k, rollback is a per-hub file revert with no re-mint because hub SKILL.md is untouched.

Plan phase 2: shrink mode-packet section 2 in ascending blast order (sk-code-quality, sk-code-ci, sk-code-skilled, sk-code-review last), keeping the three package_skill marker words inside section 2 and moving the Python block to a final machine appendix or deleting it where the hub names the leaves, leaving the EXTENSION_FLOORS block byte-identical; risk medium because leg 1b and 3 read packet routers, rollback is git revert per packet with no re-mint.

Plan phase 3: settle the sk-doc authority question with a generator rather than a decision, either generating hub-router vocabularyClasses from the 14 packet Keyword triggers lines (the only way the declared source of truth becomes true) or declaring mode-registry.json authoritative and fixing the 17 missing terms; risk high because alias churn changes live routing, rollback is reverting JSON and packet lines together.

Plan phase 4: hub SKILL.md edits come last because they are the only edits that need a re-mint and a mirror sync; replace each hub route() pseudocode with a five-line statement plus a pointer to compiled-route.cjs, keep the must-not-move rationale in one place, apply the same bytes to the .opencode mirror that build-artifacts.cjs reads, then re-mint, with compiled-route-sync.cjs --revert as rollback; risk high because a missed re-mint silently drops the hub to legacy and the mirror-sync owner is UNKNOWN.

Plan phase 5: prose pass first, contract change deferred and separate; apply the clarity rules, re-run the baseline plus verify-doc-claims.cjs, and treat any JSON-only ambition as a spec-level change that must revise RRC-001, RRC-009, the reach glob and leg 2 together rather than as a doc edit.

direction: Deliver JSON-only for hubs as a documentation change
reason: RRC-001, RRC-009, the reach glob and leg 2 all pin the hub ROUTER.md; it is a contract change (f-iter005-001).
